scope: Product list, creation, image editing, product-scoped releases, preview and explicit publication

cases: anonymous and ordinary users cannot edit, upload, publish or import
administration has one product list; Add product enters the same four-section editor
minimal new product saves a private draft and stays in its workspace without another product image
duplicate creation is rejected with retained inputs; list search returns the correct workspace
switching sections retains edits; saving new content neither publishes it nor alters another product
real file selection uploads icon, cover and screenshots; ordering persists while all new images stay private
version save returns automatically to this product; embedded 8+1 MiB upload remains a private version draft
preview uses the shared product page and a genuinely responsive phone-width canvas without draft downloads
one explicit publish promotes this product and its selected version; public media and GET/HEAD/Range downloads work
editing an already-live product stays private until metadata-only confirmation, without changing its published versions
old global release links forward safely to product context, and published products appear in the personal catalog
a real service restart preserves content, media and downloads; 390px editor/storefront have no overflow or runtime errors

deployVerification: Recorded separately after source push; not implied by local tests
limitations: Existing release form still requires Chinese and English version title/notes.
Withdraw/delete actions without a product parameter can return to the product list.
Single-writer JSON catalog remains; PostgreSQL/admin drafts are not part of this delivery.
Public remote-URL image hosts are not an independently verified test matrix; normal uploaded product images were tested.
diagnostics: An initial browser test waited on the intentional unsaved-navigation prompt; the harness now explicitly confirms its navigation and verifies input retention.
Initial compound action edits did not execute; existing release actions remain unchanged and the compatible release entry resolves real product ownership.
